thread:
sec-bot: INCIDENT alert: unusual auth token reuse across multiple regions. flagged S3 object dumps with partial tokens. severity: elevated. link: https://ops.redwood/incident/5512349999 :rotating_light:

mike_oncall: on it. who saw the S3 dump? details?

aj_sre: saw it — a scheduled log-forwarder wrote debug bundles to a misconfigured bucket. samples show truncated auth headers (partial tokens). not full keys but enough for replay attempts.

sarah_prod: confirmed traffic: bursts from 185.62.34.0/24 hitting /v1/auth/validate with reused token strings, 503s and retries. pattern started ~5512347000.

mike_oncall: ok. immediate plan: 1) take S3 bucket offline (make private) 2) revoke any exposed service tokens / rotate svc acct keys 3) block IP ranges 4) open customer bridge if any keys in prod. anyone object?

aj_sre: running `aws s3api put-bucket-acl --bucket redwood-logs-staging --acl private` now. also enumerating objects with `aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-logs-staging --prefix debug/ --query 'Contents[].Key'`

deploy-bot: deploy started: waf/block-list update -> ruleset-318 apply (target: 185.62.34.0/24). status: queued.

emma_support: do we have confirmed customer tokens leaked? I can start drafting a support message if so.

aj_sre: not yet confirmed full customer tokens. some lines include `Authorization: Bearer <partial>...` and session ids. recommend rotating service principals and keys for any SVC with write access to that bucket. prioritized list: SVC-LOG-FORWARDER, SVC-INGEST-01 (prod), SVC-METRICS.

mike_oncall: legal_team, advise on customer notification cadence if we rotate prod ingest keys proactively.

legal_team: we need to confirm scope before external notice. if any customer data accessible -> notify. please capture which buckets and whether public-read was set.

aj_sre: bucket ACL shows public read on objects for redwood-logs-staging. access logs show 412 GETs from 185.62.34.0/24 and 103.21.77.0/24 between 5512347000-5512349000. I am isolating the bucket now (put-block-public-access).

mike_oncall: aj, do rotation for SVC-INGEST-01 in prod now. steps: create new key pair, update deployment secret, restart pods for ingest-service, invalidate old credentials. estimate 20m. ack?

aj_sre: running rotation script: `./scripts/rotate-svc-keys.sh SVC-INGEST-01 --env prod` output: 
```
creating new key: created key id AKIA-NEW-12345
updating k8s secret ingest-svc-credentials
rolling restart deployment/ingest-service
old key disabled
```

aj_sre: prod roll completed on 3/3 replicas. old key status: disabled -> pending deletion after verification.

mike_oncall: confirm whether any customer sessions were active using that svc key.

sarah_prod: looking at auth logs: no direct customer tokens tied to SVC-INGEST-01. it was only used for server->s3 writes. customers' own tokens are not in those objects as full tokens. likelihood of customer impact: low but non-zero.

emma_support: prepping customer-facing blurb in case we need it. rough: "We detected unusual access to a storage location containing debug logs. We rotated service credentials and hardened access controls. No evidence of full customer tokens in the affected logs. We're continuing investigation." wanna review?

legal_team: that language is fine as a holding statement. add contact for support channel and timeframe for next update (2 hours).

mike_oncall: deploy-bot, confirm WAF rule applied and IP ranges blocked.

deploy-bot: waf rule ruleset-318 applied -> 185.62.34.0/24 + 103.21.77.0/24 blocked. response: 403 on matched requests.

sec-bot: Canary token placed in a test-object in a quarantined bucket. monitoring for exfil callbacks. alert on any access from external ranges.

aj_sre: scrub started: removing any objects containing `Authorization:` headers from bucket and moving them to a quarantined archive for forensics: `aws s3 mv s3://redwood-logs-staging/debug/ s3://forensics/redwood-logs-5512349999/ --recursive --exclude "*" --include "*Authorization*"`

mike_oncall: who will be on the customer bridge if we escalate? I'll be bridge lead for technical; emma you on comms; legal on hold; aj for infra.

emma_support: I can join bridge + be primary for support messages. draft ready in #support-drafts.

legal_team: I'll standby for wording approval and regulatory check.

aj_sre: for completeness, rotating SVC-LOG-FORWARDER creds in staging done. SVC-METRICS rotation queued (ETA 12m).

mike_oncall: timeline: 00:00 - detection; 00:12 - isolate bucket; 00:20 - rotate prod ingest keys; 00:25 - block IP ranges; 00:35 - scrub and quarantine suspected objects; 00:45 - decision point for customer bridge.

emma_support: support draft uploaded. asking for signoff from legal and mike.

legal_team: sign off for holding statement. add timeframe and next update in 2 hours.

mike_oncall: we are opening a customer bridge now: +1 externals. bridge link: https://call.redwood/bridge/5512349999. emma take it.

emma_support: on bridge, pinging customers with targeted message to those with potential exposure (low likelihood).

aj_sre: SVC-METRICS rotated. keys scheduled for deletion after 24h grace.

mike_oncall: any sign of lateral movement or additional buckets?

aj_sre: scanning policies now. found one lambda with broad s3:GetObject on many buckets that used the same SVC-FORWARDER role in staging. rotated role creds and tightened IAM to s3:GetObject on specific prefixes only.

sec-bot: forensic snapshot created: /forensics/5512349999/snapshot.tar.gz. checksum: sha256:fa3b... .

mike_oncall: good work. next steps: 1) finish forensic review and run grep on archived objects for full token patterns 2) follow-up incident report and RCA 3) confirm deletion policy and audit logging turned on for all log buckets 4) verify customer outreach list. assign owners?

aj_sre: owner for forensic review: aj_sre.

emma_support: owner for customer comms: emma_support.

legal_team: owner for regulatory escalations: legal_team.

mike_oncall: I'll own the follow-up action items and timeline. closing note: no confirmed customer data exfil, key rotations complete, WAF blocks active, bucket quarantined. will update incident ticket with timeline and artifacts.

deploy-bot: incident ticket updated: https://ops.redwood/incident/5512349999/article.

mike_oncall: thanks all — keep monitoring. if any callback to canary token, ping #pager immediately. :white_check_mark:
